correctness.rationale: The two radial profiles cross where sin(theta) sin(2u-theta)=0. In the open angular range the crossings select two antipodal arcs of each ellipse; exchange symmetry makes all four arcs congruent. Differentiation gives the stated speed and moving-limit derivative. I checked the numerator factorization exactly with symbolic expansion: for 0<t<1/2 and A>B>0 its factors are strictly positive, and both speeds are positive, giving the strict derivative sign. With W(t) the speed as a function of t=sin²(u), at perpendicularity P''=-2 W'(1/2). Half of this agrees exactly with C in RESULT.md line 29. The smooth integral even about perpendicularity eliminates cubic terms; the one-sided slope at alignment is 2(b-a) and gives a cusp on extending to signed rotations. My bounded reproduction, python /workspace/branches/replay_frozen.py 4, uses eccentric anomaly and the ordinary parametric ellipse speed rather than the source polar-speed quadrature, and also checks the symbolic certificate and coefficient. For (a,b)=(1.2,1),(3,1),(15,0.5) the approximate quadratic coefficients were 0.21161268, 2.44729996 and 1.99002659. The proof, not the samples or reported 629 diagnostics, establishes strictness and uniqueness up to symmetries. Circular, displaced, or unequal copies are not within the strict theorem.
